EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: /lwww, dilg.gov.ph DILG Legal Opinion No. 03 S. 2016 •JAN 1 2" HON. HENRY LIBREA LAQUI Vice-Mayor Mataasnakahoy, Batangas Dear Hon. Laqui: This has reference to your letters requesting the Department's confirmation of your being the Acting Mayor of Mataasnakahpy, Batangas in the meantime that the elected mayor thereat, Mayor Jay Manalo Ilagan, considered a "fugitive from justice". As culled from the documents forwarded tp the Department: On 31 March 2014, an Order of Arrest was issued by Hon. Girlie M. Borrel-Yu, Presiding Judge, Regional Trial Court, 8th Judicial Region, Branch 35, Ormoc City against Mayor Jay Manalo Ilagan for the crime of rape; On 15 December 2014, another Order of Arrest was issued by Hon. Borrel-Yu against Mayor Jay Manalo Ilagan for Violation of Section 4 (a), RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 otherwise known gs Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Person Act of 2012; On 11 December 2015, a Search Warrant was issued by Hon. Agripino G. Morga, Executive Judge, RTC, 4th Judicial Region, Branch 32, City of San Pablo finding probable cause against respondent Mayor Jay Manalo Ilagan for violation of Republic Act 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunitions Regulation Act); As represented, the Search Warrant was served at the known address of Mayor Jay Manalo Ilagan where the police forces seized therein several firearms and ammunitions. Members of the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) and other police forces also tried to serve the aforementioned Orders of Arrest against Mayor Jay Manalo Ilagan at his known address but the latter already absconded. Hence, your subject letter-requests with an information that the delivery of basic services in the Municipality of Mataasnakahoy is being hampered by the continued hiding of its elected local chief executive.

The term "fugitive from justice" was defined by the Supreme Court in Rodriguez vs. COMELEC, et al.l in this manner: To summarize, the term "fugitive from justice" as a ground for the disqualification or ineligibility ofa person seeking to run for any elective local petition under Section 40(e) of the Local Government Code, should be understood according to the definition given in the MARQUEZ Decision, to wit: A "fugitive from justice" includes not only those who flee after conviction to avoid unishment but likewise those who. after being charged. flee to avoid prosecution. (Emphasis ours. Intent to evade on the part of a candidate must therefore be established by proof that there has alrea y been a conviction or at least, a charge has already been filed, at the time of flight. xxy" (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the above-stated definition and iven the above recital of facts, it appears that Mayor Jay Manalo Ilagan can 'be coqsidered s a "fugitive from justice'! Let it be noted however that the term "fugitive from justice" is one of the grounds under Section 40 of the Local Government Code of 1991 for the disqualification or ineligibility of a candidate in a local elective office. If such evasion of warrant of arrest and thus, evasion of prosecution of charges is committed during the incumbency of the local elective official, then the relevant provision would already be Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991, which provides: "Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief' Executive. - (a) When the ov rnor ci o munici ma or or unon barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical legal reasons such as. but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-ggvernor, city or municipal vice- mayor, or the highest ranking sanggillliang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working flays." (Emphasis Supplied) As could be gleaned from the foregoing, the grounds for temporary vacancy in the office of the local chief executive are not limit d to those enumerated therein, such as 1 G.R. No. 120099, 24 July 1996.

leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. Said provision uses the phrase "such as, but not limited to "which only irpplies other similar cases. Hence, if such evasion of warrant of arre t and thus, evasion of the prosecution of the charges being committed by Mayor Jay Manalo Ilagan coupled with other circumstances (e.g. his physical absence in the office of the Mayor and his non- performance of duties as Mayor) 'Iready amounts to a temporary incapacity to perform his duties and functions, then Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 allowing you, as the duly elected Vice-Mayor of Mataasnakahoy to assume in a temporary capacity, the office of the City Mayor, may be apFlicabIe. We hope to have guided ygu accordingly. Ve truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary DILG - OUSLG 2010-01-21-002 Copy furnished: DIRECTOR ARIEL O. IGLESIA OIC.
